2.2.value: Two-part incentive fee. (2) Capital gains: 12.50% of cumulative realized capital gains since inception, net of all realized losses and unrealized depreciation, annually, less amounts previously paid. 3.8.value: ILLUSTRATIVE redemption stress test (computed for all four reference plans): base demand is each plan's filed outflow proxy (Schedule H, total expenses less administrative expenses over beginning net assets), stressed demand is the filed outflow proxy plus the increment the stress multiples add under stress (tail turnover x2, active turnover x1.5 over the slider assumption), default turnover assumptions allocation 5% of plan, tail turnover 20%/yr, active turnover 5%/yr. Global management-consulting firm profit-sharing/401(k) plan (~$9.8B, NY): filed outflow proxy 6.5% of the position per year, slider assumption 13.7%, stressed demand 19.2% vs 20% annual wrapper capacity, within wrapper capacity (19.2% vs 20%) IF offers are not prorated. US industrial manufacturer 401(k) plan (~$0.8B, OH): filed outflow proxy 11.5% of the position per year, slider assumption 7.2%, stressed demand 16.6% vs 20% annual wrapper capacity, within wrapper capacity (16.6% vs 20%) IF offers are not prorated. US casual-dining restaurant group 401(k) plan (~$1.6B, FL): filed outflow proxy 10.8% of the position per year, slider assumption 9.2%, stressed demand 18.2% vs 20% annual wrapper capacity, within wrapper capacity (18.2% vs 20%) IF offers are not prorated. US media/technology company 401(k) plan (~$570M, New York): filed outflow proxy 11.7% of the position per year, slider assumption 10.4%, stressed demand 20.5% vs 20% annual wrapper capacity, EXCEEDS annual wrapper capacity (20.5% vs 20%). Unmet demand rolls into later windows (gating-equivalent outcome). Proration assumption: an oversubscribed offer is filled pro rata and the unfilled remainder waits for the next window.

A trustee-directed sleeve could hold this wrapper directly (cell 3.5), and the daily-menu constraint applies only to the participant-directed portion, where the menu assumes daily liquidity whereas this wrapper deals quarterly with a 5% cap per quarter on outstanding shares. Facts missing for a structural verdict: gating history (12 consecutive quarterly tenders completed FY2023-FY2025 with no disclosed suspension, BUT tendered-vs-repurchased counts are never disclosed - proration cannot be ruled out from public filings, so a clean False would overclaim). The verdict stays partial until they are read from the filings. Per-plan reasons, capacity and stressed outcomes are in the liquidity match records and on the Liquidity view.

5.7.value: Anderson v. Intel Corp. Investment Policy Committee, No. 25-498 (U.S.). Certiorari granted 2026-01-16 per the Supreme Court docket listing. Question presented, per the docket as relayed in search-result snippets: whether, for claims predicated on fund underperformance, pleading that an ERISA fiduciary breached the duty of prudence requires alleging a meaningful benchmark. The Ninth Circuit had required plaintiffs to identify a comparable alternative giving a sound basis for comparison, a meaningful benchmark. No holding exists yet, and this cell draws no consequence for the evaluation. Status partial: assembled from the docket listing and search snippets, not from the source documents, which this record could not fetch.

6.1.value: Maryland corporation (formed 4/22/2020); externally managed, perpetual-life, non-traded closed-end fund electing BDC status under the 1940 Act and RIC tax status. Adviser & Administrator: Blue Owl Credit Advisors LLC, indirect affiliate of Blue Owl Capital Inc. (NYSE: OWL). Three share classes (S/D/I) plus Class I private placements to feeder vehicles. Consolidated financing subsidiaries: SPVs Core Income Funding I-X and CLO issuers (Owl Rock CLO VIII-XXII series); unconsolidated joint ventures OCIC SLF LLC (87.5% economic, co-managed with Ohio STRS) and Credit SLF; affiliated dealer manager Blue Owl Securities LLC. 6.1.source: SC TO-I, filed 2026-05-26, CIK 1812554 (with 10-K FY2025 Item 1)
6.1.quote: an externally-managed closed-end management investment company that has made an election to be regulated as a business development company under the Investment Company Act of 1940, as amended (“1940 Act”), and that is incorporated in Maryland

6.2.value: Direct origination of loans to U.S. middle-market companies (EBITDA $25M-$500M and/or revenue $125M-$5B), sponsored and non-sponsored. Portfolio at 12/31/2025 (fair value): 88.0% first-lien senior secured (40.5% of that unitranche incl. last-out), 4.2% second-lien, 1.3% unsecured, 0.4% specialty finance debt, 1.0% JVs, 1.4% preferred, 2.5% specialty finance equity, 1.2% common equity; 370 companies across 31 industries (largest: healthcare providers/services 13.9%). Complexity layers: CLO securitizations, SPV facilities, interest-rate and cross-currency swaps and FX forwards, JV structures, foreign-currency borrowings.
6.2.quote: Approximately 98.2% of our debt investments based on fair value as of December 31, 2025 are floating rate in nature, the majority of which are subject to an interest rate floor. As of December 31, 2025, we had investments in 370 portfolio companies, with an average investment size of approximately $97.1 million based on fair value.

6.3.value: Dense affiliate web: (1) SEC co-investment exemptive relief — a NEW order granted May 6, 2025 superseding the prior order, permitting co-investment with Blue Owl-managed funds on same-terms/same-time conditions with required-majority Board findings; there could be significant portfolio overlap with other Blue Owl Credit Clients as a result of the Order (filings use conditional language throughout). (3) Adviser is also the Administrator (cost reimbursement) and the CLO collateral manager (fees waived, offset if rescinded). (4) LSI Financing consulting-fee/management-fee offset.
